title: Apple's iCloud, Find My and Calendar Go Down for Users From Japan to the U.S.
text:
Apple's iCloud, Find My and Calendar Go Down for Users From Japan to the U.S. — BigGo Finance Ask AI Real-time News Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Market Influencers Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Market Influencers More Ask AI Real-time News Watchlist Holdings Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Podcast Market Influencers Apple's iCloud, Find My and Calendar Go Down for Users From Japan to the U.S.
 Add preferred source Apple's iCloud sign-in, mail, calendar, contacts, Photos and Game Center services were listed as down on the company's system status page after a disruption that began at 5:49 p.m. ET and was reflected on the Japanese, German and Australian versions of the page, pointing to a global problem. The Japanese status page recorded the start at 7:49 a.m. local time Wednesday, with six services still halted at 9:28 a.m. Find My was flagged as slow or unavailable. iCloud Drive, Keychain, Backup and iMessage kept working. Apple gave no cause or restoration estimate. Affected users reported being unable to sign in or send iCloud Mail, and some said they had been signed out of their accounts. Key Elements 
 Apple iCloud Find My iCloud Mail iCloud Calendar Game Center iCloud Drive iMessage Apple System Status Apple's iCloud services went dark for users across multiple regions on Tuesday, with the company's system status page flagging sign-in, mail, calendar and several other services as unavailable.
 The disruption began at 5:49 p.m. ET, according to Apple's System Status webpage, which listed iCloud Account and Sign In, iCloud Mail, iCloud Calendar, iCloud Contacts, Photos and Game Center as down for some users. Find My was marked as potentially slow or unavailable rather than fully offline. The same advisory appeared on the Japanese, German and Australian versions of the status page, indicating the problem was global rather than confined to one market.
 The company's Japanese-language status page recorded the start of the incident at 7:49 a.m. local time on Wednesday, and by 9:28 a.m. six services were still showing as halted for a portion of users. The outage struck at the start of the business day in Asia, a period when many users rely on iCloud Mail and Calendar to begin work.
 Not every service was caught up in the failure. iCloud Drive, iCloud Keychain, iCloud Backup and iMessage continued to operate normally, according to the status page.
 Service Status on Apple System Status 
 iCloud Account and Sign In Outage 
 iCloud Mail Outage 
 iCloud Calendar Outage 
 iCloud Contacts Outage 
 Photos Outage 
 Game Center Outage 
 Find My Slow or unavailable 
 iCloud Drive, Keychain, Backup, iMessage Operating normally 
 Note: Status reflects Apple's System Status page as of 9:28 a.m. Japan time on Wednesday.
 Apple did not immediately publish a cause for the failure or an estimate for when service would be restored. The company has not commented publicly beyond the status page updates.
 Users affected by the incident reported being unable to sign in to their Apple accounts, and some said they had been signed out of their accounts entirely. Others reported that iCloud Mail would neither send nor receive messages.
 The outage lands in the middle of Apple's fall software cycle. The company recently released iOS 27.2, an update that adds features across six of its iPhone apps, including Suggested Actions in Messages, profiles in the Apple TV app, Dual Capture for Group FaceTime calls, new Home app automation for smart locks, a split Up Next queue in Apple Podcasts and refreshed Games app tabs. None of those features appeared to be connected to the service disruption.
 For Apple, whose services segment has become a steadily growing contributor to revenue, outages of this scale carry reputational weight. Cloud-dependent features such as device backups, photo syncing and cross-device sign-in tie customers to the company's ecosystem, and extended failures can push users toward rival platforms for mail, storage and calendar functions. Investors have generally treated service disruptions as temporary operational issues rather than structural threats, though repeated incidents tend to draw scrutiny of the company's infrastructure spending.
 The status page did not indicate when engineers expected to fully resolve the problem, and it was not clear whether the outage had begun to ease by the time of publication.
